fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runlimit/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs:410-411 and attempts.rs:262-265 discard catch_unwind results. Dropping the caught Box<dyn Any + Send> runs application payload destructors outside containment. A callback using panic_any(Payload) where Payload::drop panics makes both helpers unwind. Both helpers are used by memory and PostgreSQL backends after state changes; the observer contract says telemetry cannot change admission results. This is a copy-prone catch-and-ignore pattern, not a default panic-hook concern. Two independent external characterization tests ran on Rust 1.100.0/macOS arm64 and confirmed an outer catch_unwind receives Err from each helper. Keep the fix native to Runlimit; do not add a dependency on Batter. Assess payload disposal rather than adding one more catch that can itself discard an arbitrary payload.

data.text: Cause: watchdog_tests.rs measured the 5 s bounds from spawn (FixtureChild::started), so loaded-matrix child startup consumed the unwind/exit budget. fields.description: ADR-010 recurring-defect assessment from batter-c5ci. SQLx 0.9.1 (#4514, libpq semantics) applies ambient PGHOSTADDR to every PgConnectOptions URL parse that omits hostaddr, and offers no env-free constructor or hostaddr reset. Point guards in ConnectionPlan::resolve and Runledger shared startup were followed by a second review finding the same redirect at other sites: batter-sqlx and Runlimit live-test helpers (e.g. profile_privileges_live, runlimit test_pool), Runledger drop_database after startup and the delayed-startup test, FixtureScope/FixtureSuite template initializers, scripts/test_runledger_tools.py live CLI test, and the owned_pool/verification facade examples. About 71 URL-based connection sites in ~40 files. Cause: upstream protocol change plus a Batter design gap (no library-owned URL-to-options boundary). Candidate remedy: one public batter-sqlx constructor that refuses PGHOSTADDR (and documents the process-environment precondition), adopted by every internal site and example, plus a source-inventory test like crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs forbidding raw URL parsing/connect(url) outside it; Python children scrub PGHOSTADDR. Alternative: keep SQLx 0.9.0 and request an env-free constructor upstream. Public-contract change: needs user decision.

data.text: Design assessment: the refresh inferred rustc settings from a target process and decoded the source URL through the Unix locale. Move both checks to their real boundaries. The fixture adapter copied requested TLS policy from tokio-postgres although postgres-test-harness 3d525e6 connects with NoTls. SQLx 0.9.1 applies pgpass when a parsed URL has no password and tokio-postgres distinguishes omission from an empty password on an authentication challenge. Carry the one effective transport across all fixture clients and preserve that credential distinction, refusing URL-only initializer combinations that cannot express it while keeping typed pools usable. No consumer coordination or new public API is needed.

Additional upstream evidence: SQLx 0.9.1 connection/establish.rs and connection/sasl.rs both turn a missing password into an empty challenge response. tokio-postgres 0.7.18 connect_raw.rs aborts a challenge if its password is absent. Consequently owner-login pools and initializer URLs both need an explicit password; preserve passwordless provisioning with PlannedPool::password_login by resolving that declared credential before constructing SQLx options. fields.title: Stale public OperationContext reaches probes, the fallback renderer and caller routers on in-process reuse
fields.description:
batter-nff2 refuses in-process requests carrying the adapter's private records, but a map captured behind low_level::request_admission alone carries only public values (OperationContext, RequestInterruptionResponder) and is accepted by RouterClient::request. Admitted routes are unaffected: protected admission inserts a fresh context (tested by a_map_captured_behind_request_admission_alone_carries_only_public_values). Probes and the metadata-only fallback renderer receive renderer_parts, which keeps public values, so they can see the earlier, possibly cancelled context; so can any caller-composed router read through RouterClient. Probe/fallback exposure is from code reading, not tested.

Decide per ADR-010 whether the canonical path should make this unrepresentable (e.g. HttpBoundary replacing or removing an inherited OperationContext/RequestInterruptionResponder at entry, or the entry check refusing them) or record why it is low-level caller obligation.

fields.title: observe_http without operational_http adopts an inbound CorrelationId as the completion request_id
fields.description: crates/batter-axum/src/observation.rs (observe_response) seeds ObservationState with any CorrelationId already in the request extensions. Only operational_http replaces it. Behind a RouterClient router composed with low_level::observe_http but not operational_http, a CorrelationId copied by type from an earlier request becomes the new request's completion request_id, so two requests share one correlation in telemetry. The protected boundary is unaffected because operational_http runs outermost there. Pre-existing; found by the xhigh review of PR #118.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Either observe_http never adopts an inbound CorrelationId (only operational_http sets correlation), with a test that a copied CorrelationId behind observe_http alone yields no or a fresh request_id; or observe_http's and RouterClient::request's rustdoc state this caller obligation, per ADR-010 low-level disclosure.

fields.title: Enforce that every private request record is in private_records!
fields.description:
batter-axum's renderer filter (renderer_parts) and in-process entry check (carries_private_record) are generated from the private_records! list in crates/batter-axum/src/correlation.rs. Nothing proves the list complete: a future layer that inserts a new crate-private request extension without listing it is neither stripped from renderer metadata nor refused at entry, and every test stays green (crates/batter-axum/AGENTS.md now says completeness is review-enforced). Raised in three review rounds of PR #118.

Design options considered:
- A sealed PrivateRecord trait implemented only by the macro, plus insert_private<T: PrivateRecord>(&mut Extensions, T) as the only insertion path for private records, enforced by a crate-local clippy disallowed-methods entry for http::Extensions::insert with explicit allows at public-value sites (CorrelationId, RequestId, OperationContext, RequestInterruptionResponder, response extensions). Needs a crate clippy.toml that repeats the root settings, and test-target allows.
- A source-scan test in the style of crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs. Rejected so far as fragile under rustfmt line breaks (several inserts span lines).
fields.acceptance_criteria: Inserting an unlisted crate-private type into request extensions fails clippy or a test in scripts/verify.sh; the current five records and all public-value inserts pass; a negative control (an unlisted insert) is recorded.
